author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell Brand sits down with libertarian icon Ron Paul to explore one of the most fascinating contradictions in modern politics — why young people have embraced Ron Paul as a symbol of optimism and hope when Paul himself is fundamentally pessimistic about the direction of government and human institutions. Russell and Paul dig into why this generational misreading happens and what it reveals about young people's hunger for authentic leadership in a world full of hollow political promises. A genuinely surprising conversation about perception reality and the gap between what people hear and what is actually being said.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell Brand reflects on the case of Henry Nowak and makes a powerful argument for why the right to bear arms and self-defense is not just a political issue but a matter of life and death. Russell points to America's Second Amendment as a fundamental safeguard that ensures citizens retain the ability to protect themselves when the state fails them and argues that the tragic reality of what happened to Henry Nowak is a direct consequence of a disarmed population left completely vulnerable. A raw and honest conversation about what gun control really costs ordinary people.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell Brand reacts to Liberal Democrat leader Ed Davey visiting the South Coast to hand out coffee following the party's success in the Portsmouth City Council elections and cannot hide his disbelief. Russell uses the moment to expose just how shallow and performative UK politics has become where elected officials treat serious public responsibility like a personal vanity project and celebrate minor electoral wins with PR stunts while the country falls apart around them. This is the reality of who holds power in Britain and why so many people have completely stopped trusting the political class.
